clue.text: Cross person who is …

definitions.meaning: a cross here is a hybrid animal, such as the offspring of a donkey and a horse
with the ellipsis this runs into the next clue: someone who is stubborn, a byword for obstinacy

explanation.surface: An angry person is introduced, with the sentence left hanging for the next clue to finish.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this clue to 2 Down, whose answer (stubborn) completes the second definition: a person who is obstinate.
explanation.definitionFit: The donkey-horse hybrid is proverbially stubborn, so the same word names the animal and an obstinate person.

clue.text: … this, a doubter in a frenzy

indicators.note: words in a frenzy are thrown about wildly, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: a person who is like this, a sceptic worked up into a state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this' points back across the ellipsis: the 1 Down person 'who is ... this' is stubborn. 'in a frenzy' rearranges A DOUBTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Read with 1 Down, 'this' stands for the quality of the obstinate animal, so a synonym for stubborn fits it.

clue.text: Ex-President, one in a wagon?

definitions.meaning: Jimmy, the 39th President of the United States
the driver of a cart; the question mark flags the playful reading of the word as a job title

explanation.surface: A former head of state is pictured riding in a wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: Jimmy of that surname was US President, and the same word is an old trade name for a wagon driver.

clue.text: Plant making seat messy in vehicle

indicators.note: in says the jumbled letters go inside the vehicle

parts.note: a hearse is the vehicle that carries a coffin

indicators.note: a messy seat is in disarray, so its letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Something makes a car seat untidy, perhaps a plant shedding in the back.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'vehicle' is not the car the surface suggests but a funeral carriage; 'messy' scrambles the seat's letters and 'in' puts them inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an old name for the wild pansy, a small flowering plant of the violet family.

clue.text: Trip in street like Uriah 'eep

parts.note: Uriah Heep, the fawning clerk in Dickens's David Copperfield, calls himself 'umble', humble with the H dropped, as the apostrophe in 'eep shows

explanation.surface: A fall in the road, described in the manner of Dickens's grovelling villain.
explanation.walkthrough: Uriah Heep is the obsequious clerk in Dickens's David Copperfield, forever 'ever so 'umble'; the dropped H in 'eep tells you to drop it from humble too.
explanation.definitionFit: A trip is a missed step, a near-fall, the same as a lurch over one's own feet.

clue.text: Cap all right when put wrong way round to cover top of head

indicators.note: to cover says the reversed letters go around the picked letter
put the wrong way round says the letters just given are read backwards

parts.note: OK means all right
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Wearing a cap the wrong way round is fine if it still covers the top of your head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put wrong way round' turns OKAS into SAKO, which 'to cover' wraps round H, the 'top of head'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a tall, peaked military cap, often plumed, so it is one kind of cap.

clue.text: Like something potentially shocking — terrible octet's recital

indicators.note: a terrible recital is a mess, so its letters are scrambled

parts.note: the letters of these words, the S of the possessive included, are the material

explanation.surface: An eight-piece group gives a performance so awful it shocks the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' rearranges all thirteen letters of OCTET'S RECITAL; here the possessive S counts.
explanation.definitionFit: Static electricity gives the small shock you feel from a doorknob, so a charged object is potentially shocking.

clue.text: Word of prayer finally effected change

parts.note: amen is the word said at the end of a prayer

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Saying the last word of a prayer finally brought about a change.
explanation.definitionFit: To revise or alter something, such as a text or a law, is a synonym of changing it.

clue.text: Indeed I see developments going up, just some, in area by river

indicators.note: going up says the hidden letters are read backwards
just some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone notices new building schemes going up in a riverside district.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'going up' reads the run EDISEED, from indEED I SEE Developments, bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is given to the land along the River Dee in Scotland or Wales, a district beside a river.

clue.text: Placed by entrance a superior food item

parts.note: a gate is an entrance
U stands for upper class, superior, as in 'U and non-U'

explanation.surface: A fine dish has been set down beside the doorway.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper-class, superior, comes from the 1950s 'U and non-U' classification of English usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A rich layered cream cake is a sweet food item, so the general phrase covers it as an example.

clue.text: See a rite out of place in restaurants

indicators.note: letters out of place are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone watches a ceremony that looks wrong in a dining venue.
explanation.definitionFit: A plural synonym: informal places where people go to eat are restaurants.

clue.text: One engaged to work is against going by vehicle

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
a tractor is a farm vehicle

explanation.surface: A hired worker refuses to travel by car.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm or person hired under agreement to do a job is engaged to work on it.

clue.text: Discouraging message conveyed by digital means

definitions.text: Discouraging message conveyed by digital means

parts.words: Discouraging message conveyed by digital means
parts.note: 'digital' suggests computers but means by the fingers: a gesture with the thumb pointing to the floor signals disapproval

explanation.surface: An off-putting reply arrives by email or text.
explanation.walkthrough: 'digital' suggests computers, but a digit is a finger or thumb, and this gesture of rejection is made with one.
explanation.definitionFit: A turned-down thumb is the gesture of rejection, so it is a discouraging sign made with a digit.

clue.text: Edge of dress getting grease and grime

indicators.note: edge of here picks the final letter of the word dress

parts.note: oil is a grease or lubricant

explanation.surface: The hem of a dress gets stained with oily dirt.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean dirt that marks a surface, as with soiled clothing smeared with filth.

clue.text: Loose human, he'd somehow become famous person

indicators.note: somehow says these letters get put together in some other way

explanation.surface: A free-spirited man has somehow risen to celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: A person known in every home is a celebrity, someone famous enough to be recognised by everyone.

clue.text: Times in which number will get gongs for achievements?

indicators.note: in which says the second piece sits inside the first

parts.note: hours are times of day

explanation.surface: Asks at what point a certain figure will be given medals for what they have done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gongs' is British slang for medals and decorations.
explanation.definitionFit: Awards such as knighthoods given in the New Year and Birthday lists are decorations for achievement.

clue.text: Misgivings about the French garments of an earlier time

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: doubts are misgivings
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Someone has reservations about the old-fashioned clothes of the French.
explanation.definitionFit: Close-fitting jackets worn by men from the 14th to 17th centuries are clothes of a bygone era.

clue.text: Head of Society and VIP who looks down on the lesser orders?

definitions.text: who looks down on the lesser orders?

indicators.note: head of picks the first letter of the word Society

parts.note: a nob is a toff, a person of rank

explanation.surface: A society figure and a grandee look down on the working classes.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who scorns people of lower social standing is the textbook social elitist.

clue.text: Old fellow makes one muse with health amiss

indicators.note: amiss means gone wrong, so the letters are put into a different order

explanation.surface: An ailing body makes a person think deeply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'muse' looks like a verb meaning ponder, but it is just letters to rearrange with HEALTH.
explanation.definitionFit: This Biblical patriarch lived 969 years, making him the proverbial very old man.

clue.text: Male bore lacking substance maybe

parts.note: an eagre is a tidal bore, a wave surging up a river

explanation.surface: A tedious man may be rather shallow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bore' is not a dull person but a tidal wave up a river, called an eagre on the Trent.
explanation.definitionFit: Something scanty or thin, such as a scant meal, lacks substance, hence the 'maybe'.

clue.text: Entertain a goddess

parts.note: the Muses were the nine Greek goddesses of the arts

explanation.surface: A command to host a deity.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep people diverted or make them laugh is to entertain them.

clue.text: Designer hugs a doctor, one of four in a circle

definitions.text: one of four in a circle

indicators.note: hugs means wraps arms round, so the first piece goes around the rest

parts.note: Mary Quant was the British fashion designer of the miniskirt era

explanation.surface: A fashion designer embraces a medic, one of four friends sitting in a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: Mary Quant was the London fashion designer of the 1960s known for the miniskirt.
explanation.definitionFit: A circle divided by two perpendicular diameters gives four equal quarter-sections, each named with this term.

clue.text: Legal termination of protocol — terrible

indicators.note: the termination of a word is its final letter

parts.note: awful means terrible

explanation.surface: Ending a diplomatic procedure is lawful but dreadful.
explanation.definitionFit: Permitted or allowed by the law means the same as legal.

clue.text: Colourful herb and egg in a sandwich?

indicators.note: in says the egg letter sits inside the other piece

parts.note: wad is British slang for a sandwich or bun; the question mark admits the stretch
O looks like an egg in shape

explanation.surface: A snack of salad leaves and egg in a sandwich.
explanation.walkthrough: WAD is old British forces slang for a bun or sandwich.
explanation.definitionFit: This plant of the cabbage family yields a blue dye, famously used by ancient Britons, hence colourful.

clue.text: One joining up for work in channel

definitions.meaning: a person who stitches cloth together, a needleworker
a drain or conduit carrying waste water

explanation.surface: A recruit signs up for a job in a waterway.
explanation.walkthrough: Read one way it is someone who sews; read another, a drain.
explanation.definitionFit: The same letters spell a needleworker and, pronounced differently, an underground drain for waste water.

clue.text: Salt — it is packed in box

indicators.note: is packed in says the first word goes inside the box

parts.note: a crate is a box for transport

explanation.surface: Some salt has been packed into a container for shipping.
explanation.definitionFit: In chemistry it is a salt or ester of citric acid, so salt is the general class.
